findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Evidence claim: `_DCInbound` is a thin wrapper over `inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields` (not a separate implementation), and `_DCSanitizer` delegates to shared `jira_family` sanitizers — only `_map_local_to_dc_fields` and the `WikiTextCodec`-parameterized portions of `_DCSanitizer` are genuinely DC-specific; scope AC1-AC2 to those two only.
evidence: backend.py:116-119: `def map_remote_to_local(self, remote_fields): from rebar_reconciler import inbound_fields; return inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields(remote_fields)` — identical call to what Cloud makes
backend.py:127-149: _DCSanitizer delegates to `_shared_sanitize_label`, `_shared_sanitize_summary`, `_shared_sanitize_description`, `_shared_sanitize_comment` from jira_family
Plan quote: '_DCOutbound, _DCInbound, _DCSanitizer are separate implementations from Cloud's, not thin wrappers'
findings.finding: The Evidence section claims `jira_datacenter/backend.py:68-153 — _DCOutbound, _DCInbound, _DCSanitizer are separate implementations from Cloud's, not thin wrappers.` Reading the file refutes this: `_DCInbound.map_remote_to_local` (backend.py:116-119) is a one-line delegation to `inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields(remote_fields)` — the same function Cloud uses — making it a thin wrapper, not a separate implementation. Similarly, `_DCSanitizer` delegates entirely to shared `jira_family` sanitizers with injected codec parameters. Only `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (and the WikiTextCodec-parameterized portions of `_DCOutbound`/`_DCSanitizer`) are genuinely DC-distinct. This false assertion in the Evidence section could lead the implementer to write DC-specific characterization tests for `_DCInbound` (e.g., map_remote_to_local value pins) expecting DC-unique behavior, when in fact those assertions would be characterizing the shared `inbound_fields` module's behavior, not anything DC-specific — producing redundant tests rather than a genuine DC safety net.
findings.location: Evidence section: `jira_datacenter/backend.py:68-153 — _DCOutbound, _DCInbound, _DCSanitizer are separate implementations from Cloud's, not thin wrappers.`
scenarios: Implementer writes DC-specific value pins for `_DCInbound.map_remote_to_local`, expecting them to cover DC-unique logic, when they actually pin shared `inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields` behavior already covered by Cloud characterization tests.
Implementer over-counts what needs to be independently characterized for DC, inflating the test suite with redundant assertions that don't close the stated asymmetry gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Revise the Evidence bullet to read: '`_DCOutbound.map_local_to_remote` (via `_map_local_to_dc_fields`) and `_DCSanitizer`'s WikiTextCodec-parameterized description/comment methods are DC-specific; `_DCInbound` and `_DCSanitizer.sanitize_summary`/`sanitize_label` delegate to shared `jira_family` implementations identical to Cloud's and need no DC-specific value pins beyond what AC2 already specifies.'

findings.finding: The Evidence section claims `_DCInbound` is a 'separate implementation from Cloud's, not thin wrappers', but the actual code shows `_DCInbound.map_remote_to_local` (backend.py:116-119) is exactly a thin wrapper that delegates verbatim to `inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields` — the same function Cloud's inbound uses. This factual inaccuracy in the plan's Evidence could mislead the implementer into believing DC's inbound mapping differs from Cloud's and warrants its own characterization pins, or alternatively cause confusion about why `_DCInbound` is absent from all ACs.
findings.location: Evidence section: 'jira_datacenter/backend.py:68-153 — _DCOutbound, _DCInbound, _DCSanitizer are separate implementations from Cloud's, not thin wrappers'
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Evidence bullet to: '`jira_datacenter/backend.py:68-153` — `_DCOutbound` and `_DCSanitizer` are separate DC implementations; `_DCInbound` is a thin wrapper that delegates to the shared `inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields`, identical to Cloud\'s inbound path and out of scope for DC-specific pins.'

findings.finding: The plan states '_DCInbound … [is a] separate implementation from Cloud's' (Evidence section: 'jira_datacenter/backend.py:68-153 — _DCOutbound, _DCInbound, _DCSanitizer are separate implementations from Cloud's, not thin wrappers'). In reality, _DCInbound.map_remote_to_local (jira_datacenter/backend.py:116-119) delegates directly to inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields — the identical function Cloud's inbound mapper calls. _DCInbound is a thin wrapper over shared logic, not a separate implementation. This incorrect premise could lead the author to write DC inbound characterization pins (e.g. testing _map_jira_to_local_fields outputs) that duplicate Cloud's existing inbound pins rather than exposing a distinct DC code path.

The plan's Evidence section asserts `jira_datacenter/backend.py:68-153` — `_DCOutbound`, `_DCInbound`, `_DCSanitizer` are 'separate implementations from Cloud's, not thin wrappers.' The actual code refutes this: `_DCInbound.map_remote_to_local` delegates directly to `inbound_fields._map_jira_to_local_fields` (the same function Cloud uses); `_DCSanitizer` delegates entirely to shared `jira_family` sanitizers; `_DCOutbound.map_fields_to_remote` is a single-line delegation to `OutboundFieldMapper`. These are thin delegation wrappers by the plan's own definition. The premise inflates the scope of genuinely DC-specific pinning needed.

AC5 offers two equally-weighted seam options ('EITHER by calling classify_probe_response directly OR by constructing a JiraDataCenterTransport over a stub jira.JIRA-shaped client') without selecting one, but the choice is load-bearing: test_jira_family_seam.py:164-194 already pins all four probe branches AND the custom resolved_statuses injection via option (a) (direct classify_probe_response calls). If the implementer uses option (a), they will duplicate existing coverage that is already passing, producing tests that cannot add mutation-catching power. Option (b) (JiraDataCenterTransport over a stub client) is the only option that pins the DC TRANSPORT's wiring — that the transport correctly threads its _resolved_statuses into classify_probe_response — which is the genuinely uncovered gap.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Revise AC4 to clarify that DC uses the IDENTICAL `JiraIdentityConvention` as Cloud (backend.py:225), so no DC-distinct value pin is possible or needed; instead, scope the identity coverage to verifying the delegation wiring (that `JiraDataCenterBackend.identity` IS a `JiraIdentityConvention` instance), or drop AC4 from the DC parametrization and note that identity is already covered by Cloud's existing pins on the shared class.
evidence: JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__ line 225: `self.identity = JiraIdentityConvention()` — same class as Cloud
test_backend_characterization.py:255-279 already pins every branch of JiraIdentityConvention by value through Cloud's _backend()
Plan states: 'where Cloud and DC legitimately differ, the parametrization carries a DIFFERENT expected value per vendor'
Plan states: 'Every assertion here should be one a wrong-but-well-formed value fails' — but an identity assertion through DC's backend cannot fail differently from Cloud's
findings.finding: AC4's mechanism ('DC's identity label form is pinned by value') cannot achieve its stated goal because JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__:225 wires `self.identity = JiraIdentityConvention()` — the IDENTICAL class Cloud uses, not a DC-specific implementation. Writing DC identity pins in the parametrized suite produces assertions byte-for-byte identical to Cloud's existing pins (test_backend_characterization.py:255-279). This contradicts the plan's own principle: 'where Cloud and DC legitimately differ, the parametrization carries a DIFFERENT expected value per vendor' — there is no difference to carry for identity. Furthermore, any mutation that broke the identity behavior would be caught by Cloud's existing pins; the DC parameter adds zero net mutation-detection coverage. An implementer following AC4 as written will either produce a test that passes vacuously (because it asserts the same thing as Cloud's already-passing pins) or will be confused about what DC-specific value to pin.
scenarios: Implementer writes DC identity assertions with the same expected values as Cloud — the tests pass but add zero discriminating coverage and the mutation-check log will show the DC identity test and Cloud identity test fail together, not independently.
Implementer tries to find a DC-specific expected value for identity label form and cannot, causing confusion or a mis-specified test.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace AC4 with: 'DC's identity wiring is confirmed: assert `isinstance(JiraDataCenterBackend(transport=FakeTransport()).identity, JiraIdentityConvention)`. No value-level pin is added because DC and Cloud share the same `JiraIdentityConvention` class verbatim — Cloud's existing value pins in test_backend_characterization.py:255-279 already cover every branch of that shared class, and a duplicate assertion through DC's backend cannot fail independently.'

The choice affects AC8's proving target: if parametrized, the existing Cloud assertions live in the same file and must survive edits; if split, the Cloud file is untouched and AC8 is trivially true without running anything
findings.finding: The file-structure decision (parametrized single file vs. a split sibling) is deferred to the executor with no stated criterion for when the threshold 'turns out to obscure the Cloud pins' is crossed, leaving a real architectural choice open mid-task.
findings.location: Scope section: 'decide by trying the parametrization first; a split is the fallback, not the default'
scenarios: An executor who never reaches the 'parametrize first' breakpoint defaults to a split unnecessarily, silently weakening the AC8 safety-net story
An executor who parametrizes but misjudges the obscuring threshold ships a harder-to-read file without the plan's blessing to split
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence such as: 'Split if and only if the parametrization requires conditional branches (if vendor == DC) inside a test function body; otherwise keep one file. Under both paths, AC8 is verified by running pytest on the Cloud-containing file with no diff to its existing assertions.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify AC2: replace 'both DC sanitizer boundaries' with either the exact count of distinct numerical limits (e.g. 'all DC sanitizer size limits') or name each limit constant explicitly, so implementers know how many boundary values to pin across the three listed fields.
evidence: 'both DC sanitizer boundaries are pinned at-limit AND one-over, including the truncation suffix marker, for summary, description and comment'
ABSENCE: the plan body never states how many distinct size constants DC's sanitizer defines, so 'both' cannot be resolved from context
findings.finding: AC2 says 'both DC sanitizer boundaries are pinned at-limit AND one-over … for summary, description and comment' — the word 'both' implies exactly two boundary values, but three fields are listed. An implementer cannot determine from the text whether there are two distinct numerical limits (applied across three fields) or three separate limits (making 'both' incorrect), nor which fields share a limit if there are only two. This ambiguity could cause a pin to be omitted silently.
scenarios: Implementer assumes two boundaries and skips the comment boundary, producing a gap that AC2 was meant to close.
Implementer assumes three boundaries and invents a spurious third limit not in the code, producing a brittle test.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'both DC sanitizer boundaries' with 'all DC sanitizer size limits' (or 'each of the DC sanitizer's size limits') and, if the limits for summary/description/comment are distinct constants, list them by name; if summary and description share one constant and comment has another, state that explicitly.

findings.finding: The mutation-checking requirement ('perturb the value it pins… and confirm that pin — and ideally only that pin — goes red. Record the verdicts on the ticket') has no automated proving command and lacks the `[operator-attested]` tag required by the OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE to classify out-of-repo evidence as sufficiently specified. As written, there is no way to verify from the closing PR's CI or any repo artifact that mutation-checking was performed. The word 'here' in 'Record the verdicts on the ticket' is also ambiguous (ticket comment? PR description? test-file docstring?).
findings.location: Testing section — 'Record the verdicts on the ticket'; AC7 — 'every new pin is mutation-checked, with the mutation and the resulting verdict recorded here'
findings.suggested_fix: Prepend `[operator-attested]` to the mutation-checking AC and add: 'Evidence: a single ticket comment in the format: `MUTATED: <constant> <old_value>→<wrong_value>; FAILED: <test_id>` for each pin, posted before the PR is merged.'

findings.finding: 'Record the verdicts on the ticket' makes the mutation-check AC's done-evidence a one-time ticket annotation rather than a durable repo artifact, so it cannot be verified via CI or repo inspection after the session — it is post-session-only attestable.
findings.location: Testing section / 'Record the verdicts on the ticket'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a docstring or inline comment block in the test file recording each pin's mutation result; this makes the evidence a committed repo artifact reviewable in the PR diff.
